docs.title: District Administrator Quick Start
docs.text:
Version 1.1.002 — Review Edition

Use this site to manage schoolboard.net user accounts and group memberships. District Administrator role assignments are controlled by schoolboard.net Support.

On a smaller screen, select ☰ Topics to open the documentation menu.

docs.title: 1. Find the user
docs.text: Search People before creating or changing an account.

docs.title: 2. Manage the account
docs.text: Add or edit only the approved account information.

docs.title: 3. Assign the group
docs.text: Add the existing user to the correct Board or committee group.

docs.title: 4. Verify access
docs.text: Confirm status, roles, memberships, and private-material access.

docs.title: Common workflow
docs.text:
1. Sign in with your individual District Administrator account.
  2. Select Manage, then People.
  3. Search for the username or email address before creating an account.
  4. Select Add user when no account exists.
  5. Enter a unique email address and username, set the initial password, select Active, and create the account.
  6. Open Groups, select the correct group, and open Members.
  7. Select Add member, choose the existing user, and assign Group Admin only when approved.
  8. Save and verify the account, role, and membership.
  9. When access must stop, block the account and confirm its status.

Use least access

Add only the roles and memberships the person needs. Never share an administrator account for testing.

District Administrator role requests

Only schoolboard.net Support can add, delete, or modify a District Administrator role assignment, including removing the role from an account. Submit every request in writing by email to schoolboard.net Support. There is no system limit, but schoolboard.net recommends only two or three District Administrators per district.

docs.title: Administration access
docs.text: Use the administration toolbar to reach account and group management.

docs.title: Open the toolbar
docs.text:
1. Sign in with your assigned District Administrator account.
  2. Select Manage.
  3. Select People for user accounts or Groups for group membership.
  4. Use Back to site to return to the public-facing district site.

Figure SB-DST-002. District Administrator toolbar.

Confirm the site

Administrator pages can change access to private materials and site configuration. Confirm the district site and account before making a change.

docs.title: Block and restore access
docs.text: Blocking is the preferred review-draft procedure when access must be suspended but the account and history should be retained.

docs.title: Block accounts
docs.text:
1. Open People and find the user.
  2. Confirm the username and current Active status.
  3. Select the correct account checkbox.
  4. Select Block the selected user(s) from Action.
  5. Confirm that only intended accounts are selected.
  6. Select Apply to selected items.
  7. Refresh or filter the list and verify Blocked status.

Figure SB-DST-022. Block selected user accounts.

docs.title: Restore access
docs.text: Use Unblock the selected user(s) only after approval. Review roles and group memberships before unblocking.

docs.title: Offboarding sequence
docs.text:
1. Block the account promptly.
  2. Remove unnecessary Group Administrator access and email schoolboard.net Support when the District Administrator role must be removed or modified.
  3. Remove group memberships when approved.
  4. Preserve or reassign content according to district policy.
  5. Cancel the account only when an approved procedure requires it.

docs.title: Find Missing Content or Agendas
docs.text: District Administrators can use Content to search the complete site-wide content list, including items that do not appear on the expected group page.

docs.title: Search the Content list
docs.text:
1. Select Manage, then Content.
  2. Search by title or part of the title.
  3. Filter by content type or publication status when useful.
  4. Sort by Updated, or scroll through the list.
  5. Review the assigned Group, author, status, and updated date before opening the item.

Before recreating an agenda, always check the Content list to determine whether it already exists.

docs.title: Choose the newest revision
docs.text: When revisions are enabled, several entries may have the same title. Compare the Updated date and time and open the most recent entry. Confirm its publication status and assigned Group. Do not delete older entries until the current published version has been confirmed.

docs.title: Verify the Group assignment
docs.text:
Every agenda must be assigned to the intended Board or committee group. An agenda assigned to the wrong group—or to no group—may disappear from the expected group page, be unavailable to its Group Administrator, or fail to reach the intended notification audience.

Correct the Group assignment and verify the agenda from the group page before recreating content.

Fastest first check

For “Where did my agenda go?” questions, check Content, the newest Updated date, publication status, and assigned Group first.

docs.title: Conventions Used in This Guide
docs.text:
This guide uses consistent information boxes to distinguish instructions from operational and security guidance.

Tip or Best Practice

A recommended method that improves consistency or reduces avoidable work.

Note

Helpful background information or a related detail.

Important

A step that deserves particular attention to avoid an access or content problem.

Warning or Security Restriction

A security, privacy, or access risk. Stop and verify authorization before continuing.

docs.title: Using this guide on a phone or tablet
docs.text:
1. Select ☰ Topics in the upper-left corner to open the guide menu.
  2. Select a topic.
  3. Select the page-outline icon on the right side of the topic title to open the page Table of Contents.
  4. Select a heading to move directly to that section.

Questions are encouraged

If a direction, permission, or request is unclear, ask before continuing. There are no stupid questions.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
The Groups list shows group ID, name, type, publication status, owner, and available operations.

Figure SB-DST-012. Groups list.

docs.title: Review a group
docs.text:
1. Confirm the group name and type.
  2. Open the group's operation menu or open the group.
  3. Select Members.
  4. Review existing members before adding another user.

docs.title: Add a group
docs.text:
1. Select Add group from the Groups page.
  2. Select the group type only after confirming its intended audience and access.
  3. Enter the approved group name and details.
  4. Save and verify the group.
  5. Add approved members and Group Administrators.

docs.title: Choose the correct type
docs.text:
• Board Groups are public-facing groups for published agendas and related content.
  • District Groups are internal groups without a public presence.
  • No Private File Access supports internal review of shared content without access to private attachments.

Group Type cannot be changed

A group's type cannot be changed after creation. If the wrong type is selected, create a new group using the correct type and move content under an approved plan.

ATM is already provided

Do not create another ATM (Administrative Team) group. schoolboard.net provisions ATM as a No Private File Access group and assigns the designated District Administrator during setup. Email schoolboard.net Support to request administration or membership changes.

docs.title: Group memberships
docs.text:
Use a group's Members tab to review, add, edit, or remove membership.

Figure SB-DST-014. Group membership list.

docs.title: Add an existing user
docs.text:
1. Confirm that the account exists and is active.
  2. Open the correct group and select Members.
  3. Select Add member.
  4. Begin entering the username and select the correct autocomplete result.
  5. Leave URL alias empty unless the district has an established reason to use it.
  6. Select Group Admin only when approved.
  7. Select Save and verify the Members list.

Figure SB-DST-016. Add an existing user to a group.

docs.title: Edit a membership
docs.text:
1. Open the operation for the correct member and select Edit.
  2. Select or clear Group Admin according to approved access.
  3. Leave URL alias unchanged unless a documented requirement applies.
  4. Select Save and verify the role.

Figure SB-DST-017. Open the membership Operations menu.

Figure SB-DST-018. Edit a group membership.

docs.title: Remove a membership
docs.text:
1. Confirm the username and group.
  2. Open the membership operation and select Remove.
  3. Read the confirmation.
  4. Select Delete to remove the membership or Cancel to leave it unchanged.
  5. Verify the Members list.

Figure SB-DST-020. Remove a group membership.

Membership versus account

This procedure acts on the group membership. It is separate from blocking or cancelling the user account. Reviewers should confirm that the confirmation wording is sufficiently clear.

docs.title: People and users
docs.text:
The People page displays usernames, status, roles, account age, last access, and available operations.

Figure SB-DST-004. People list and account controls.

docs.title: Find an account
docs.text:
1. Enter part of the username or email address in Name or email contains.
  2. Optionally select a Status, Role, or Permission filter.
  3. Select Filter.
  4. Confirm the username, status, roles, and last access before editing.

docs.title: Work safely
docs.text:
• Select the username to review an account.
  • Select Edit in Operations to change one account.
  • Select checkboxes only when applying a bulk action.
  • Confirm the selected-account count before applying an action.
  • Do not cancel accounts until the district approves when cancellation is appropriate.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Active An account status that permits sign-in when other access requirements are satisfied.

Blocked An account status that prevents sign-in while retaining the account record.

District Admin A site role for approved district-level administration. Only schoolboard.net Support can add, remove, or modify the role, and every request must be submitted in writing by email. There is no system limit, but schoolboard.net recommends two or three District Administrators per district.

Group Admin An administrative role associated with group management. Confirm whether the intended workflow assigns it as a site role, membership role, or both.

Group membership The relationship that places an existing user in a specific Board, committee, district, or access-control group.

docs.title: Reviewer confirmation requested
docs.text:
1. Is blocking the preferred reversible offboarding action before cancellation?
  2. Does removing a membership leave the user account and content intact?
  3. Is the schoolboard.net Support-only District Administrator role procedure clear and consistent with district authorization practices?

The Add Group procedure is documented from the Groups page. Content-list screenshots previously labeled SB-DIS-023 and SB-DIS-024 must use the corrected SB-DST-023 and SB-DST-024 names when added to the repository.

docs.title: Roles and access
docs.text: Review site roles and group memberships separately. Use the least access required for the person's assignment.

docs.title: Role guidance
docs.text:
• District Admin is for approved district-level administration. Only schoolboard.net Support can add, delete, or modify a role assignment, including removing the role from an account.
  • Group Admin is for approved group-management functions allowed by site configuration.
  • An ordinary Board Member generally needs the correct group membership, not a site-wide administrator role.

District Administrator role requests must be emailed

A district user, Group Administrator, or District Administrator cannot add, delete, or modify a District Administrator role assignment. Send every request in writing by email to schoolboard.net Support. Include the district site, person's name, username or email address, requested change, effective date, and the authorized district requester.

docs.title: Recommended number of District Administrators
docs.text:
There is no system limit on the number of District Administrators. For clearer accountability and reduced security risk, schoolboard.net recommends limiting each district to two or three District Administrators.

Review the list when responsibilities change. Email schoolboard.net Support promptly when the role must be added, removed, or modified.

docs.title: Least-access sequence
docs.text:
1. Start with the ordinary user account.
  2. Add only required group memberships.
  3. Add Group Admin only when the person must manage the group.
  4. When District Administrator access is required, obtain district approval and email the written request to schoolboard.net Support.
  5. Test with the user's own account; never share administrator credentials.

Group Administrator changes

Follow the approved group-membership workflow for Group Administrator access. The schoolboard.net Support-only restriction applies specifically to the District Administrator role.

docs.title: Administrator safety
docs.text:
• Use individual accounts and multifactor authentication when available.
  • Apply the least access needed for the person's job.
  • Confirm selected usernames before bulk actions.
  • Never send passwords through ordinary email.
  • Block access promptly when authorization ends.
  • Record who approved District Admin and Group Admin access.
  • Send every District Administrator role request in writing by email to schoolboard.net Support.
  • Review District Administrator assignments periodically and keep the recommended total to two or three per district.
  • Review administrator assignments periodically.

docs.title: Keyboard and accessibility
docs.text:
• Press Tab and Shift+Tab to move through controls.
  • Press Enter to open links or activate focused controls.
  • Use the visible focus indicator to confirm the current control.
  • Use form labels and headings with a screen reader.
  • Increase browser zoom when needed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Problem What to check User cannot sign in Username, email address, status, and identity before resetting a password Private material is missing Membership in the correct group User has too much access Site roles and every group membership Account already exists Edit the existing account; do not create a duplicate Membership removed accidentally Add the existing user back to the approved group Group type is unclear Stop and ask the site owner or support team Agenda is missing from a group Search Content, choose the newest revision, and verify the assigned Group

When requesting help, include the site address, username, group, expected result, actual result, and a screenshot with passwords and private information removed.

docs.title: Security Policies
docs.text: These procedures provide a written authorization trail for district-wide administrative access.

docs.title: District Administrator accounts
docs.text:
Only schoolboard.net Support can add, remove, or modify District Administrator access. Submit every request by email from an authorized district representative. Include the district and site, administrator name, username or email, requested action, effective date, and authorized requester.

schoolboard.net recommends maintaining two or three District Administrators for continuity while keeping district-wide access limited.

docs.title: ATM (Administrative Team)
docs.text:
Every site is provisioned with an ATM (Administrative Team) group using the No Private File Access group type.

  • Administrators do not need to create this group.
  • During setup, schoolboard.net assigns the designated District Administrator as a Group Administrator of ATM.
  • Requests to change ATM administration or membership must be submitted by email to schoolboard.net Support for security documentation.
  • ATM members may review shared content but cannot view private attachments.

Do not create another ATM group

Use the provisioned ATM group. Email schoolboard.net Support when its administration or membership must change.

docs.title: Group types are permanent
docs.text: A group's type cannot be changed after creation. If the wrong type is selected, create a new group using the correct type and move content according to an approved plan. Always confirm the intended type before saving a new group.

docs.title: Add and edit users
docs.text: Search before creating an account. Email addresses and usernames must be unique.

docs.title: Add a user
docs.text:
1. Open People and select Add user.
  2. Enter the person's Email address.
  3. Enter a unique Username.
  4. Enter the initial password in Password and Confirm password.
  5. Confirm that the passwords match.
  6. Select Active unless access must remain unavailable.
  7. Select Notify user of new account only when the email address is verified and the account is ready.
  8. Leave optional settings at district defaults unless a documented requirement applies.
  9. Select Create new account.
  10. Search for the username and verify the result.

Figure SB-DST-006. Add user form.

Group access

Creating the account does not necessarily provide access to private Board materials. Add the user to each approved group separately.

docs.title: Edit a user
docs.text:
1. Find the correct account on People.
  2. Select Edit.
  3. Change only fields supported by an approved request.
  4. To reset a password administratively, enter the new value in both password fields.
  5. Use Status to select Active or Blocked.
  6. Select Save and verify the People list.

Figure SB-DST-008. Edit user account.

Account cancellation

Cancel account is separate from blocking and may be destructive depending on site configuration. This review draft recommends blocking when reversible suspension is sufficient.
